capability.vault_panel: An authenticated Chrome extension reads Mine and Shared masked item summaries and origin-matched saved logins. For a supported focused login page, the Vault site section offers Sign in, which calls credential_login.run({action:'auto', credential_item_id}) through useCredentialLogin.
capability.agent_tool: credential_login action=list returns metadata-only inventory and action=discover returns field names; action=auto uses the extension-assigned tab, not an agent-supplied URL. The live tool binding is documented for the extension, but no callable Vault/credential connector is exposed to this Codex task.
capability.credential_boundary: The handler checks a real extension user token, HTTPS destination, top frame, origin consistency and safe form submission before materialization. The server rechecks item access, browser_fill_enabled and URL matching. Plaintext stays inside the handler's fill call and tool results contain status and non-secret metadata only.
capability.chrome_profile_boundary: The side panel and assigned tab must be in the same Chrome profile. The already admin-authenticated primary extension cannot fill a tab in a separate test profile.

evidence_gap: No dedicated Vault MCP connector is available in this task's callable tools.
No Vault inventory or item title was read, so no saved test@test.com item, access grant, browser_fill_enabled setting or matching login URL is established.
No browser or login was launched under this lane; no secret, session, account or role was read or changed.
next_guarded_execution: After the root's browser and resource guard admits a run, use an isolated Chrome test profile. Authenticate its extension to an account authorized for a clearly designated test@test.com Vault item, and select an organization on that device. Do not use the primary admin profile for this test.

In that same profile, open the existing real web login at https://www.aimatrx.com/login and focus its login form. Open Vault in the actual side panel. Inspect only masked item titles and the origin-matched list; select Sign in only if a clearly designated test@test.com item is shown and enabled for this page. The item title alone is a lead, not identity proof.

Let the Vault Sign in action complete the normal form submission. Verify the website account through its authenticated identity view, then perform the extension's real Sign in flow and verify the extension resolves test@test.com with admin=false. For organization cases choose one of the principal's live member-role organizations, not an owner/admin-role organization.

If no designated matching item exists, if its actor cannot use it, or if the login cannot establish the test identity, stop the member acceptance attempt as an access gap. Do not reveal/copy a password into a transcript, inject a session, create or modify a principal, change a role or alter a Vault item to force the test.
limitations: Vault matching proves that an actor may use an item on an origin; it does not prove the saved credential belongs to test@test.com. Website and extension identity must be checked after the action.

The Vault Sign in button is conditional on a supported Chrome build, safe focused top-frame login, page status ready and a matching saved item. A child-frame login may offer a separate Fill button; that is not the same automatic submit path.
An authenticated website session does not by itself establish a member extension session. The extension OAuth result must be observed separately.
